title: Recent Trends in Physics — 40 MCQs
description: Covers elementary particles and antiparticles, classification of particles, quarks and their charges, quark compositions of mesons and baryons, leptons, Big Bang theory, Hubble’s law and expansion of the universe, dark matter, black holes and gravitational waves.

questions.q: An antiparticle has the same mass as its corresponding particle but
options: opposite charge and opposite other quantum numbers
questions.explanation: Every particle has an antiparticle with identical mass but opposite electric charge and opposite values of other additive quantum numbers.

questions.q: The antiparticle of the electron is the
questions.explanation: The positron (e⁺) is the antiparticle of the electron.

questions.q: Quarks are the fundamental constituents of
questions.explanation: Hadrons (baryons and mesons) are composed of quarks.

questions.q: The charge of an up quark is
questions.explanation: The up quark (u) carries electric charge +⅔ e.

questions.q: The charge of a down quark is
questions.explanation: The down quark (d) carries electric charge −⅓ e.

questions.q: Leptons are particles that
options: do not participate in strong interactions
questions.explanation: Leptons interact via electromagnetic, weak and gravitational forces but not via the strong force.

questions.q: An example of a lepton is the
questions.explanation: The electron is a fundamental lepton.

questions.q: Hubble’s law states that the recessional velocity of a galaxy is proportional to its
questions.explanation: v = H₀ d, where d is the distance of the galaxy from the observer.

questions.q: The Big Bang theory describes the
options: origin and evolution of the universe
formation of the solar system only
questions.explanation: The Big Bang model is the prevailing cosmological theory of the origin and expansion of the universe.

questions.q: A black hole is a region of spacetime from which
options: nothing, not even light, can escape
questions.explanation: The escape velocity at the event horizon exceeds the speed of light, so nothing can leave a black hole.

questions.q: The quark composition of a proton is
questions.explanation: A proton consists of two up quarks and one down quark (uud).

questions.q: The quark composition of a neutron is
questions.explanation: A neutron consists of one up quark and two down quarks (udd).

questions.q: A meson is composed of
questions.explanation: Mesons are quark-antiquark bound states.

questions.q: A baryon is composed of
questions.explanation: Baryons (protons, neutrons, etc.) are three-quark states.

questions.q: The positively charged pion π⁺ has the quark content
questions.explanation: π⁺ = u d̄ (up quark and anti-down quark).

questions.q: The six flavours of quarks are
options: up, down, strange, charm, top, bottom
up, down, electron, muon, tau, neutrino
proton, neutron, pion, kaon, lambda, sigma
photon, gluon, W, Z, graviton, Higgs
questions.explanation: The six quark flavours are u, d, s, c, t and b.

questions.q: Which of the following is a lepton?
questions.explanation: The muon (μ⁻) is a charged lepton.

questions.q: According to Hubble’s law, a galaxy at a distance of 100 Mpc with H₀ = 70 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ has a recessional velocity of
Dark matter is called “dark” because it
questions.explanation: Dark matter does not interact electromagnetically and therefore neither emits nor absorbs light.

questions.q: Gravitational waves are
options: ripples in spacetime produced by accelerating masses
electromagnetic waves of very long wavelength
sound waves in the interstellar medium
questions.explanation: Accelerating masses (especially compact binaries) generate propagating distortions of spacetime called gravitational waves.

questions.q: The event horizon of a black hole is the surface at which
options: escape velocity equals the speed of light
questions.explanation: At the event horizon the escape velocity equals c; nothing can cross it outward.

questions.q: The antiparticle of a proton is the
questions.explanation: The antiproton (p̄) has the same mass as the proton but opposite charge (−e).

questions.q: Evidence for the expansion of the universe includes
questions.explanation: The cosmological redshift of galaxies is a direct observational consequence of the expansion of space.

questions.q: The charge of a strange quark is
questions.explanation: The strange quark (s) has electric charge −⅓ e.

questions.q: Hadrons are classified into
questions.explanation: Hadrons that feel the strong force are subdivided into baryons (three quarks) and mesons (quark-antiquark).

questions.q: A galaxy is observed to have a recessional velocity of 14000 km s⁻¹. Taking H₀ = 70 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ its distance is
The quark composition of the positive kaon K⁺ is
questions.explanation: K⁺ consists of an up quark and an anti-strange quark (u s̄).

questions.q: The total electric charge of a uud combination is
questions.explanation: Charge = (+2/3) + (+2/3) + (−1/3) = +1 e, which is the charge of the proton.

questions.q: The total electric charge of a udd combination is
questions.explanation: Charge = (+2/3) + (−1/3) + (−1/3) = 0, corresponding to the neutron.

questions.q: Pair annihilation of an electron and a positron at rest produces two photons each of energy approximately
questions.explanation: Each photon carries the rest energy of one particle, 0.511 MeV.

questions.q: The existence of dark matter is inferred mainly from
options: galactic rotation curves that remain flat at large radii
direct detection of photons from it
questions.explanation: Stars in the outer parts of galaxies orbit faster than can be explained by visible matter alone, indicating additional unseen mass.

questions.q: Gravitational waves were first directly detected by LIGO from the merger of
options: a black hole and a star
questions.explanation: The first detection (GW150914) was the merger of two stellar-mass black holes.

questions.q: The Hubble constant H₀ has dimensions of
questions.explanation: H₀ = v/d so its SI unit is s⁻¹ (or km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹).

questions.q: A particle that is its own antiparticle is the
questions.explanation: The photon (and also the Z⁰ and π⁰ under certain conditions) is identical to its antiparticle.

questions.q: The Big Bang model predicts that the universe was once
questions.explanation: Extrapolation backward in time leads to a hot, dense early state from which the universe expanded.

questions.q: The cosmic microwave background radiation is considered strong evidence for the Big Bang because it is
options: the cooled remnant of the early hot universe
questions.explanation: The nearly isotropic 2.7 K black-body radiation is the redshifted afterglow of the early hot phase.

questions.q: A black hole of solar mass has a Schwarzschild radius of approximately
questions.explanation: R_s = 2GM/c² ≈ 3 km for M = M_☉.

questions.q: The lepton number of an electron is +1. The lepton number of a positron is
questions.explanation: Antiparticles carry the opposite lepton number; the positron has L = −1.

questions.q: Which combination of quarks has a total charge of zero and can form a baryon?
questions.explanation: udd has charge 0 and is the neutron; uuu and ddd would have charges +2e and −e respectively and are not the ordinary neutron.

questions.q: If the Hubble constant were larger, the estimated age of the universe would be
questions.explanation: In the simplest approximation the age is ∼1/H₀; a larger H₀ implies a younger universe.
